about: Replayable orchd tasks: each starts at the parent of a commit that already solved it; `reference` is that commit, for comparison only. Mixed sizes: mechanical, standard, UI and daemon. Kept small: run it before a flag becomes a default or after a big harness change; day-to-day A/B runs on real backlog requests. `check` grades a finished task: orchd runs it from the root of a throwaway worktree at the task's final commit and the task counts as a success only when it exits 0. Each check overlays the reference commit's own test on the result and runs it by exact name, so a run that matches no test fails. A task whose `check` calls a function names that function in its request, so the grade measures behaviour, not a guessed name.

tasks.name: attempt-counter
tasks.request: The orchestrator task detail header shows 'attempt N/M' where N is the daemon's global attempt number across plan, implement and review stages, so a task on its first implementation attempt can read 'attempt 3/4'. Make it count implementation attempts only, in the header and wherever the panel counts attempts toward the limit; cover it in tests/orchestrator-helpers.test.cjs. The graded interface: the exported helper `attemptProgress(task, maxAttempts?)` in src/orchestrator/helpers.ts stays the one place that builds the 'N/M' text (e.g. "1/4"; null when the task is not running or queued), and tests call it directly.
tasks.check: git show 0ed5678:tests/orchestrator-helpers.test.cjs > tests/zz-ref-check.test.cjs && node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^(attemptProgress counts the implement attempt while running or queued, null otherwise)$' tests/zz-ref-check.test.cjs | grep -qx '# pass 1'

tasks.name: unfenced-json
tasks.request: Codex sometimes drops the backticks around its final sushi-report or sushi-review block and sends the bare tag line followed by the JSON; orchd then finds no report or no verdict. Parse that form too, keep fenced blocks working, and add a unit test built from such a reply.
tasks.check: { echo '#[cfg(test)] mod ref_check { use super::*; use crate::model::*; #[test]'; git show 98481f2:orchd/src/brief.rs | awk '/fn a_reply_that_drops_the_backticks_still_parses/{p=1} p{print} p&&/^    }$/{exit}'; echo '}'; } >> orchd/src/brief.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet ref_check::a_reply_that_drops_the_backticks_still_parses 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 1 passed'

tasks.name: base-branch-field
tasks.request: In the orchestrator panel's '+ New task' form (src/orchestrator/OrchestratorPanel.tsx), add an optional base branch field so a task can start from another branch; it is passed as `base` to task.create (orchd already accepts it) and defaults to the repo's current branch. Show the branch a task started from (task.baseRef) in the task detail header. Prove the form and the header with screenshots saved under artifacts/. The graded interface: an exported helper `taskCreateParams(params, base)` in src/orchestrator/helpers.ts returns the task.create params plus a trimmed `base` only when the base is not blank (no `base` key at all otherwise), and tests call it directly.
tasks.check: git show 7110044:tests/orchestrator-helpers.test.cjs > tests/zz-ref-check.test.cjs && node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^(taskCreateParams adds a trimmed base on the request path, omits the key when blank|taskCreateParams adds a trimmed base on the title/goal fallback path too)$' tests/zz-ref-check.test.cjs | grep -qx '# pass 2'

tasks.name: task-costs
tasks.request: orchd task costs are too low: the plan run and the review run report a cost that is never added to the task, and Codex runs report tokens but no cost at all. Add plan and review costs to the task total, price Codex runs from per-model prices kept in settings (with built-in list prices for the Codex models in use), and make `orchd ab` leave out tasks created before variants existed so they don't skew the default arm.
tasks.check: git show 8c5fd73:orchd/tests/integration.rs > orchd/tests/zz_ref_check.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet --test zz_ref_check -- --exact the_planner_s_tier_routes_the_task_only_when_the_variant_asks_for_it 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 1 passed'
